<!-- generated by scripts/cli-reference.mjs from `goback docs`; do not edit -->

Back up and restore MySQL 5.5 through 8.4 servers: dumps and the binary log, each in a set of its own

```sh
goback [global flags] mysql <command>
```

## mysql receive

receive connects as MySQL's option files say: the [client] group of --defaults-extra-file and
~/.my.cnf, for host, port, socket, user, password and ssl-mode. The user needs REPLICATION SLAVE and
REPLICATION CLIENT. It starts at the newest dump's binlog, so take a dump first. After RESET MASTER
the binlogs go on in a new chain of the same set.

```sh
goback [global flags] mysql receive [flags]
```

| Flag | Description | Environment | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--spool value` | directory binlogs wait in for their commit | `GOBACK_MYSQL_SPOOL` |  |
| `--dump-set value` | set the server's dumps go to |  |  |
| `--defaults-extra-file value` | MySQL option file read before ~/.my.cnf, for the connection and its password | `GOBACK_MYSQL_DEFAULTS_EXTRA_FILE` |  |
| `--server-id value` | replica server id to connect with; one derived from the set's name by default |  |  |
| `--commit-every value` | how often new binlog is committed; at least 10s |  | `1m0s` |
| `--commit-bytes value` | how much new binlog makes the receiver commit early |  | `256MiB` |
| `--window value` | how far back point-in-time recovery reaches; binlogs older than the oldest dump inside it are let go |  | `336h0m0s` |
| `--shutdown-grace value` | how long the last commit may take after SIGTERM |  | `30s` |

## mysql dump

The client programs connect as MySQL's option files say: ~/.my.cnf, or --defaults-extra-file.
With log_bin on, the dump records the binary log position it is consistent with.

```sh
goback [global flags] mysql dump [flags]
```

| Flag | Description | Environment | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--binlog-set value` | set the server's binlogs go to, whose chain the dump joins |  |  |
| `--no-binlog-position` | record no binary log position even with log_bin on: no global read lock, no RELOAD or REPLICATION CLIENT |  |  |
| `--defaults-extra-file value` | MySQL option file the client programs read before their own, for the connection and its password; ~/.my.cnf alone when empty | `GOBACK_MYSQL_DEFAULTS_EXTRA_FILE` |  |
| `--mysql value` | the mysql client to run | `GOBACK_MYSQL` | `mysql` |
| `--mysqldump value` | the mysqldump to run | `GOBACK_MYSQLDUMP` | `mysqldump` |
| `--mysqlbinlog value` | the mysqlbinlog a restore replays with; at least the source server's version | `GOBACK_MYSQLBINLOG` | `mysqlbinlog` |

## mysql restore

The client programs connect to the target as MySQL's option files say: ~/.my.cnf, or
--defaults-extra-file. --to only writes the dump and the binlogs into a directory and prints
the commands that apply them.

```sh
goback [global flags] mysql restore [flags]
```

| Flag | Description | Environment | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dump-set value` | set the server's dumps go to |  |  |
| `--binlog-set value` | set the server's binlogs go to, for restoring past the dump |  |  |
| `--at value` | moment to restore to, as RFC 3339 (2026-10-02T14:30:00Z), to the second; the end of the binlog set when empty |  |  |
| `--to value` | empty directory to write the dump and the binlogs into instead of applying them |  |  |
| `--work-dir value` | directory the binlogs are fetched into before the replay; the system's temporary directory when empty |  |  |
| `--force` | load into a server that holds databases already |  |  |
| `--defaults-extra-file value` | MySQL option file the client programs read before their own, for the connection and its password; ~/.my.cnf alone when empty | `GOBACK_MYSQL_DEFAULTS_EXTRA_FILE` |  |
| `--mysql value` | the mysql client to run | `GOBACK_MYSQL` | `mysql` |
| `--mysqldump value` | the mysqldump to run | `GOBACK_MYSQLDUMP` | `mysqldump` |
| `--mysqlbinlog value` | the mysqlbinlog a restore replays with; at least the source server's version | `GOBACK_MYSQLBINLOG` | `mysqlbinlog` |
